deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a student-style set of notes from a mineralogy or crystallography lecture, probably from Riemann's student years around 1853 (the folio is headed 'Riemann 26' and numbered 26 by the author). The content is purely descriptive, and there is nothing to restate in formulas.

The page begins in the middle of a classification of 'Abänderungen' (modifications) of a simple crystal form. In these modifications an edge or corner (Ecke) of the form is replaced by new faces. The previous item, presumably 'Abstumpfung' (truncation, i.e. replacement by one face), is on an earlier page.

(a) Zuschärfung (bevelling): the part is replaced by two new faces that meet each other in an edge. On edges this can be 'gerade' (straight, symmetric) or 'schief' (oblique).

(b) Zuspitzung (acumination, pointing): the part, typically a corner, is replaced by three or more new faces. This gives an 'x-flächige Zuspitzung' (x-faced acumination), with the new faces set either against the edges or on the faces of the original form.

(c) Modifications of different kinds can be combined, e.g. bevelling of the edges together with truncation of the corners.

Next comes a new heading: 'Krystallsymmetrie oder die Gesetzmässigkeit in der Construction der Krystalle' (crystal symmetry, or the regularity in the construction of crystals). The symmetry shows itself in the following respects:

1. The crystal faces are distributed uniformly around a line. The centre of gravity (Schwerpunkt) of the crystal body falls on this line. One may think of the crystal form as developed about this line, and it is called the axis of the crystal form.

For the so-called closed ('geschlossene', underlined) forms, the position of this axis is given: it passes through the two opposite terminal corners (Endecken).

The page breaks off at 'Bei Entwicklg d.'. The next page continues: in describing crystals one places the axis vertically, and this orientation is called the normal position.

This is the standard Weiss/Naumann-style morphological crystallography taught in German universities in the 1840s–50s. No computation is performed.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page is descriptive. As a description it is loose. The 'axis' is described as a line about which faces are 'uniformly distributed', and the centre of gravity of the crystal is said to lie on it. This is a heuristic lecture formulation, not a precise symmetry-axis definition. It also does not hold for, e.g., triclinic forms, which have no such axis.

results.what: Terminology for modifications of crystal forms: Zuschärfung (two new faces meeting in an edge, straight or oblique) and Zuspitzung (three or more new faces, set against edges or on faces). These can be combined with Abstumpfung.
results.modern_name: Morphological description of combination forms (truncation, bevelment, acumination) in classical crystallography
results.usually_credited_to: Werner/Weiss/Mohs/Naumann tradition of German mineralogy (late 18th to early 19th century)

results.what: Crystal symmetry introduced via a principal axis around which faces are uniformly distributed. For closed forms the axis passes through two opposite terminal corners and is placed vertically ('normal position').
results.modern_name: Principal (main) crystallographic axis / orientation convention for crystal description
results.usually_credited_to: Christian Samuel Weiss (axis systems, 1815) and Carl Friedrich Naumann (textbooks)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine lecture notes on elementary crystal morphology, standard German mineralogy-course material of the time. There is no mathematics, and nothing beyond the textbook content of the era. Its only interest is biographical: it documents that Riemann attended or studied mineralogy and crystallography.
transcription_corrections: Header line: the folio number written at top right is '216' (folio number), not '26'.

Line 4: the image reads 'Zuspitzung, wo d. Theil ersetzt d. drei oder mehr neue[n] Flächen ersetzt ist (x flächige'. The duplicated 'ersetzt' is in the original, but the first 'ist' in the machine transcription is spurious.
'Krystallsymmetrie oder die Gesetzmässigkeit / in der Construction d. Krystalle' is a centred section heading.

Item 1: 'in diese der Schwerpunkt der Krystallkörper fallen' is plausible but uncertain; possibly 'in welche'. The phrase 'welche man sich als d. Axe der Krystallform entwickelt denken kann' is uncertain in the image. It may read something like 'um welche man sich d. Krystallform entwickelt denken kann'.
'geschlossenen' is underlined in the original ('sog. geschlossenen Formen').
Last line: 'indem sie d. zwei entgegengesetzten Endecken geht. Bei Entwicklg d.' is confirmed. Here 'd.' before 'zwei' stands for 'durch'.
